newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault half-year sales rise 6.3 percent.
newsitem.headline: Renault half-year sales rise 6.3 percent.

text.p: French carmaker Renault SA reported on Wednesday that its half-year sales rose 6.3 percent as an increase in exports more than compensated for the weakness in its home market.

Renault said turnover grew to 100.04 billion francs ($15.9 billion) in the first six months of the year from 94.09 billion, helped by the performance of the Megane and other new models and by sterling's rise against the French franc. On a like for like basis, sales rose 5.1 percent, it said in a statement.
The figures were in line with expectations after Renault's domestic rival, PSA Peugeot Citroen, reported a 6.3 percent rise in its half-year sales to 94.64 billion francs in late July.
Shares in Renault closed down 2.14 percent at 164.40 francs, swept lower in a selloff that took the Paris bourse down 2.5 percent.

The rise in Renault sales was generated almost entirely by the car business, whose revenues rose to 80.09 billion francs from 74.53 billion despite a 23.7 percent slump in first-half car sales in France from artificially inflated year-earlier levels.

"The gain was due primarily to an improvement in the model mix resulting from the success of the Megane, but also the new Safrane, the new Espace, and a gain in sales volumes of Renault outside France," the company said.
It said currency movements, notably the pound's rise, also boosted results in the car division.
Renault said its car sales in the rest of Europe rose 13 percent in the first half of the year, more than twice as fast as the six percent growth rate for car sales in Europe excluding France.
Its share in Britain -- where it is the leading importer -- grew to 7.3 percent from 6.5 percent, increasing the benefits of sterling's 16.5 percent appreciation against the franc this year.
Renault is also the leading importer in Germany, where its market share rose to 6.2 percent from 5.5 percent.

Its strong commercial performance reflects the success of the mid-sized Megane, notably the phenomenally popular minivan-styled Scenic version which is the top selling car in France and fifth in Europe.

Sales in Renault's truck business rose 3.5 percent to 15.93 billion francs, as higher billings by Mack Trucks in the United States and a rise in the dollar more than offset lower truck sales in Europe.
Finance division revenues, mainly interest payments on loans to finance sales, slipped 3.2 percent to 4.03 billion francs due to lower interest rates.
